why: 0.66.0 was packed from the full working tree and shipped 42 internal docs (474 files). Every earlier release shipped ~432. 0.66.1 rebuilds from the reduced public tree that GitHub carries, so GitHub, npm and GitLab describe the same thing.
runtimeDelta: none — the only file present in 0.66.0 and absent in 0.66.1 is CHANGELOG.md

defectsFoundByThisRelease.what: contracts/*/LOCK.json hashed raw bytes while core.autocrlf rewrites line endings on checkout, so a fresh clone failed check:contracts on every file
defectsFoundByThisRelease.fix: the lock hashes CRLF-normalised text; verified in a worktree whose checkout really is CRLF (73 CRLF in schema.json)
defectsFoundByThisRelease.whyItEscaped: the first verification ran in the dirty working tree that had produced the locks, not in a clean checkout

defectsFoundByThisRelease.what: two tests assumed the full tree: the vendored-runtime allowlist required a fixture that the public tree does not contain, and a fixture restore re-serialised JSON instead of restoring the exact bytes
defectsFoundByThisRelease.fix: an allowlist entry applies only where its file exists; restore by exact bytes

twoRepoRule.github: core code + bilingual README + LICENSE only; no experiment archives, no changelog, no process documents
twoRepoRule.gitlab: the whole project including docs/experiments (472k lines), process notes and the changelog

installedInto.method: the Electron app owns this profile, so dsh plugin add refuses; the dependency was pinned and `pnpm install` run in place
verified: taskAttribution reachable from the installed package

notVerified: The Tasks panel was not opened in the running app: a dsh-purge consent modal covers the UI and accepting it is the owner's decision, not the agent's.
No task row was created to show the new line with real data.
Windows installer and Remote Agent were not rebuilt (Remote Agent stays 0.1.1).
